notes: Ethereum mainnet (chain 1), contracts-only launch. Changes made: only this launch.json was added; no contract logic, fee numbers, roles, limits, events or configuration files were changed. Deploy exactly the four listed constructors, in order, with zero ETH and no initialization calls. 1. KeelToken(): the locked EIP-1167 clone template; its constructor marks the template initialized so it cannot be used directly. 2. KeelVault(owner_=$owner). 3. KeelFactory(owner_=$owner, vault_=KeelVault, tokenImplementation_=KeelToken, hookSaltStart=0): the constructor only checks that vault_ and tokenImplementation_ are non-zero, mines the CREATE2 salt on chain with HookMiner.find starting at 0 until the KeelHook address carries C.HOOK_FLAGS, deploys KeelHook(factory, vault) itself, and records it in the immutables hook, hookSalt and hookSaltAttempts while emitting HookDeployed(hook, salt, attempts). Do not deploy KeelHook separately; it is not a manifest entry. The salt search cost depends on the factory's own address, so simulate this constructor in the resolved deployment context before sending it: tests measured about 6 million gas. 4. KeelRouter(owner_=$owner, factory_=KeelFactory). KeelFactory.paused is true at construction and stays true after deployment; nothing here unpauses it. The owner then completes setup with separate transactions, in order: KeelVault.wire(KeelFactory), KeelFactory.setSigner, KeelFactory.setStartTickBounds, KeelVault.setVerifier, KeelRouter.setEthPool, then KeelFactory.setPaused(false), using the owner's chosen values. Publish the confirmed deployed addresses of KeelToken, KeelVault, KeelFactory, KeelHook and KeelRouter from the deployment handoff; read KeelHook from KeelFactory.hook() and confirm it against the HookDeployed event in the factory's creation receipt. This manifest asserts no mainnet addresses.
